articleTitle: YOLOv5-based Foreign Object Detection Algorithm for Transmission Lines
abstract: To address the problem of low detection accuracy of foreign objects on transmission lines using the YOLOv5 algorithm, this thesis proposes a transmission line foreign object detection algorithm based on YOLOv5. The CSP-DarkNet53 backbone network is replaced with an improved lightweight Mobilenetv2 structure to reduce the computation of training the network and improve detection speed. The SENet attention mechanism model is integrated, and deeper downsampling is added to the feature extraction module to improve the recognition accuracy of small targets in transmission line foreign objects. The experimental results show that the mAP of the improved model proposed in this paper reaches 91.6%, which is 4.5% higher than that of the original model.

articleTitle: Research on the Prediction of Benign and Malignant Ovarian Tumors Using Improved ResNet
abstract: With the wide application of deep learning in medical image analysis, the prediction of benign and malignant ovarian tumors has become an important research direction in the medical field. This study improves ResNet (Residual Networks) to improve its accuracy in the prediction task of benign and malignant ovarian tumors. Firstly, we introduce parallel downsampling and CBAM hybrid attention mechanism, which enables the model to capture a wider range of contextual information and enhances the model's attention to important features, improving the ability to extract information from key areas of ovarian tumors. Secondly, through the improved activation function layer, we optimize the efficiency of feature information transmission, making the model better adapt to the nonlinear characteristics of ovarian tumor images. In addition, we adopt an appropriate data augmentation strategy to expand the training dataset, improve the generalization performance of the model, and provide more reliable support for the accurate diagnosis of ovarian tumors.

articleTitle: Classification of Alzheimer's Disease Using fMRI-Based Brain Functional Network Data
abstract: In recent years, functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) has played a crucial role in revealing brain functional networks, especially in the study of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Given the successful application of deep learning techniques in medical image analysis, this study proposes a hybrid model combining Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory networks (Bi-LSTM), and Multi-head Attention mechanisms to improve the classification accuracy between AD and normal controls (CN). By taking functional connectivity (FC) network matrices as input, our model not only enhances sample diversity with Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) but also effectively extracts spatial and temporal features through improved 1D CNN and Bi-LSTM. Importantly, the Multi-head Attention mechanism enables the model to adaptively and parallel learn the importance of features at different time steps and spatial locations in the sequence. Experimental results show that our model achieves a high accuracy of 98.59% in the classification task between AD and CN, demonstrating the potential of this method in early diagnosis of AD.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Flowmeter Signal Processing Based on Wavelet Noise Reduction
abstract: The electromagnetic flowmeter on the dredger is prone to significant fluctuations in flow value, resulting in considerable measurement error and a lack of precision in the measurement results, this study proposes an electromagnetic flowmeter signal processing method based on wavelet noise reduction. By analyzing the interference conditions affecting the dredger's electromagnetic flowmeter during usage, we introduce a wavelet noise reduction method with an improved threshold function. This function is adept at handling smaller signals; when the wavelet decomposition coefficient falls below the threshold, it is not directly set to zero. Instead, by adjusting the parameters, a superior noise reduction effect is achieved, which subsequently enhances the measurement precision of the electromagnetic flowmeter. Experimental results indicate that compared to traditional measurement methods, the accuracy of measuring cumulative flow rate is improved by 2.23%-4.5%. The wavelet noise reduction technique with the refined threshold function can effectively mitigate noise interference, resulting in more precise measurement outcomes.

articleTitle: Community Detection Algorithm based on Graph Capsule Networks
abstract: GNN (Graph Neural Network) is a type of neural network model specifically designed to handle graph-structured data. Compared to traditional neural network models such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), GNN aims to process data with nodes and edges to capture the relationships and structure among nodes in a graph. However, existing GNNs have limited capabilities in obtaining hierarchical graph representations, which are crucial for graph classification. To address the limitations of GNNs, this paper proposes an improved graph capsule network that incorporates a data disentanglement module to recover the underlying independent factors from observed mixed data, thus unraveling the heterogeneous factors behind node embeddings. By extracting node features in the form of capsules and utilizing routing mechanisms, important information at the graph level can be captured. This allows for the decomposition of the feature representation of each node into independent representations corresponding to different factors or attributes, enabling a better understanding and utilization of the diverse features of nodes and enhancing the effectiveness and capabilities of graph analysis and learning.

articleTitle: Blurring Degree Calculation from Single Microscopic Defocused Image Based on Adaptive Spectral Clustering
abstract: Deconvoluting a defocused image with a degradation function, also named as point spread function, is an effective method for image de-blurring. However, the blurring kernel of a point spread function is highly susceptible to various disturbances such as image texture, brightness, and noise due to the complex imaging mechanism in high-magnification optical microscopes, and it is difficult to fast and accurately obtain the point spread function of a defocused microscopic image. In this paper, the relationship between point spread function in the blurring imaging process and image similarity function in adaptive spectral clustering (ASC) is analyzed, and a defocused image classification method according to the blurred degree of each image is proposed based on ASC. Subsequently, a normalized blurring degree estimation method for single microscopic blurred image is proposed based on ASC combined with the K-nearest neighbor method, and the point spread function denoted as a Gaussian function can be obtained with the blurred kernel value. Finally, experiments based on the nanoscale square grid proves the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Multi-Robot System Simulate Design Based on Player/Stage
abstract: multi-robot technology is an important branch of robotics, and its research results are widely used in all walks of life. The open-source robot simulation platform Player/Stage has rich functions, strong operability and development. In this experiment, Player/Stage is used to carry out the secondary development of the robot simulation platform. In this study, the simulation platform Player/Stage is used to simulate multi-robot systems in a virtual environment, communicate through TCP socket technology to control clients, and design and write executable files such as word files and cfg files and client control programs. The client robot optimized its action path using the Dijkstra algorithm and successfully avoided obstacles. Finally, simulation experiments and debugging are carried out, and a typical multi-robot motion system simulation is successfully realized. The feasibility of combining global path planning and local path planning has been verified.

articleTitle: Enhanced YOLOv5 for Traffic Object Detection: Combined Channel Attention and Spatial Attention Mechanism
abstract: Autonomous driving technology has brought the challenge of efficient and accurate detection to the forefront. To address this, this paper presents an improved YOLOv5 model by incorporating channel attention and spatial attention to stabilize the detection of pedestrians, vehicles, traffic lights, and traffic signs. Attention mechanism has been proven beneficial in improving many networks. The traditional YOLOv5 network lacks attention mechanisms, this research focuses on how to add appropriate attention mechanisms at relevant positions. This allows the network to learn channel importance weights and attend to spatial locations that require attention. In this research, the improved YOLOv5 model was performed in a rearranged BDD100k dataset, with the first 20,000 images of the original dataset as the training set and the first 6,000 images of the original dataset as the validation set. Results demonstrates that the proposed model significantly outperforms the baseline in several aspects. Notably, it achieves an increase of 5.1% in precision and an improvement of 1.3% and 0.1% in mAP@.50-.95 and mAP@.50 respectively. Comparison experiment on the VOC2007 dataset indicates that the model can improve 0.4% in recall and 0.2% in mAP@.50-.95 with the maintaining of precision. Experimental results validate the combination of various attention mechanisms could enhance model precision and mAP with the performance in the scene of complex traffic object detection.

articleTitle: Knowledge Graph Completion Method based on Two-level Attention to Aggregate Neighborhood Multimodal and Type Features
abstract: The current research of knowledge graph completion usually considers various factors such as entity types and multimodal features. However, only considering entity types may blur the selection of entities due to the incomplete predefined entity types in the knowledge graph. Although multimodal features can enrich the semantics of entities, it may bring noise and redundant information affecting the representation effective. Therefore, we propose a knowledge graph completion method which comprehensively considers the entity types and text-image multimodal features to enhance the embedding representation of entities. Firstly, the features of triples, entity types and text-image are extracted respectively. Then, the structural representation with type constraints is obtained by adding the features of triples and types, and the multimodal fusion representation is obtained by weighted average of the features of text and image. Furtherly, we propose a two-level attention mechanism of relation and entity to aggregate entity neighborhood information including structural representation and multimodal representation, which can obtain more accurate and rich entity and relation embedding representations in different contexts. Experiments on both FB15K-237 and self-constructed domain dataset show that the proposed method outperforms the baselines.

articleTitle: A relocalization method based on 3D features
abstract: The handheld three-dimensional (3D) scanning system requires relocalization when the system’s pose is incorrect caused by matching failures. This paper proposes a relocalization method based on 3D features, which utilizes voxel downsampling to obtain 3D key points and constructs 3D features with Fast Point Feature Histograms (FPFH) descriptors. A series of keyframes are defined based on differences between frames. A coarse-to-fine point cloud registration strategy is employed for matching with these keyframes, as well as a frame skipping matching trick to accelerate the matching process. Experimental results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method for relocalization in handheld 3D scanning systems, and the average matching frame amount is reduced to about 50%, and the time consumption is reduced by about 40%.

articleTitle: Pedestrian Object Detection Based on Transformer Architecture
abstract: The current common object detection models are all based on convolutional neural network architectures. Although these models have good detection performance, their complex structures make it difficult to scale up and deepen. This paper proposes an object detection model based on the Transformer architecture, which can make fuller use of image features compared to models based on convolutional neural network architectures. Experiments on the coco2017 dataset show that the model proposed in this paper achieves 17.7% in AP_small and 38.7% in AP_0.5:0.95, improving small object detection by 4.9% and overall detection performance by 5.8% compared to the original DETR. The detection performance of the model proposed in this paper is the best compared to previously proposed object detection models. In practical detection in a campus environment, it can accurately detect objects in situations with large objects, small objects, and obstructions, and it is less likely to miss small objects in obstructed conditions.

articleTitle: Infrared and Visible Image Fusion Method Based on Infrared Mask and Attention Mechanism
abstract: In order to solve the problem that the main target is missing and the texture details are not clear in the current infrared and visible image fusion methods. This paper proposes an infrared and visible images fusion method based on infrared mask and attention mechanism. This paper uses infrared mask images and its anti -images as a loss of fusion images to ensure that fusion images can retain more effective information about source images. In order to retain more effective information and details in source images, this paper introduces spatial attention mechanism. Spatial attention and infrared mask together assist infrared and visible image fusion. The training and comparison experiments are carried out on the MARS public dataset, and the generalization test experiments are carried out on the RoadScene public dataset. The subjective and objective evaluations are carried out on the two datasets respectively. The experimental results show that the proposed method can retain more effective information and details in the source image and make the target in the fused image more prominent.

articleTitle: The Vision State Space Model Based on Triplet Attention Mechanism
abstract: In the realm of AI modeling, the accuracy, efficiency, and adaptability of visual state space models in complex environments have remained paramount areas of research. This paper proposes a novel Triplet Attention Mechanism to enhance the model's performance in processing visual information. To validate the effectiveness of this triplet attention mechanism in visual information processing, a combination of theoretical analysis and experimental validation is employed. The paper initially delves into the working principles of the Triplet Attention Mechanism and its contribution to improved model performance. The advantages of visual state space models are then explored. Subsequently, the paper outlines the specific implementation steps of the Triplet Attention Mechanism, encompassing the construction of the attention model, its integration into an existing visual state space model, and the optimization of parameters to achieve optimal performance. Experimental results demonstrate that the visual state space model integrated with the Triplet Attention Mechanism exhibits superior accuracy and efficiency compared to models utilizing traditional attention mechanisms. The paper concludes by emphasizing the significance of the Triplet Attention Mechanism in the application of visual state space models and envisioning its promising future in the field of visual information processing.

articleTitle: Design and Research of Robot Digit Recognition Based on Yolov5 and OCR
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the detection speed and accuracy are difficult to maintain a high level at the same time in the process of elevator button recognition, this paper proposes a YOLOv5+OCR elevator button recognition model. The YOLOv5 network detection scale and prediction output are improved, and the OCR branch is introduced to improve the network feature extraction ability. Different data sets are used to verify the feasibility of YOLOv5+OCR model, and the performance of the model is verified by comparing with other models. Experimental results show that the model has good performance in recognition accuracy and recognition speed, which can effectively improve the efficiency of robot elevator button recognition.

articleTitle: Integrating Reality: Exploring the Application Prospect of VR Technology in Physical Education Teaching
abstract: With the continuous progress of technology, virtual reality (VR) technology has been gradually introduced into the field of physical education and has become a cutting-edge tool for innovative teaching methods. With the title "Integrating Reality: Exploring the Application Prospect of VR Technology in physical education" as the starting point, this study discusses the practical application potential, advantages and challenges of VR in physical education. Based on the methods of literature review and case analysis, and referring to the National Virtual Simulation Experimental Teaching Course Sharing platform (www.ilab-x.com), this paper further studies the specific application of VR technology in different sports such as golf, football and archery, and evaluates its impact on students' skill improvement, strategy understanding and psychological training. The research results show that by providing an immersive learning environment and simulated training conditions, VR technology can significantly improve students' participation, enhance skill acquisition, and enhance psychological endurance. In addition, VR can provide a safe and easily accessible training environment, which is particularly suitable for beginners and students with physical limitations. Despite the challenges in terms of cost, hardware compatibility and user comfort, this study believes that VR technology has broad application prospects in physical education teaching with further development of the technology and cost reduction.

articleTitle: Systematic Analysis of Underwater Image Dehazing and Object Detection
abstract: Dehazing underwater images is crucial for several underwater applications, including marine biology, exploration, and monitoring. Because of colour distortion, light attenuation, and scattering, underwater imaging presents particular difficulties. This research presents a systematic survey on using transformers and different Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) for dehazing underwater photos. This survey study looks into transformer-based models, analyzes GAN designs (CycleGAN, Pix2Pix, and UWGAN) in detail, and compares them using a range of metrics, such as Mean Squared Error (MSE), Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM), Frechet Inception Distance (FID), and F1-score. Further analysis was carried out using CLAHE on the best-performing models. Our findings emphasize the benefits and drawbacks of the different designs that were employed as well as prospective directions for further study and advancement.

articleTitle: Automatic Modulation Recognition Method Based on Short-time Fourier Transform and Vision Transformer
abstract: In the rapidly evolving landscape of wireless communication technology, the increasing number of wireless communication devices has led to high spectrum utilization rates. To effectively monitor and manage wireless communication, this paper proposes an automatic modulation recognition (AMR) method based on the short-time fourier transform (STFT). Through STFT, communication signal features can be effectively extracted and converted into feature maps. A method of overlapping block processing is proposed, combined with Vision Transformer (ViT), to identify the modulation scheme of the signal. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed architecture, based on STFT and VIT, achieves a modulation classification accuracy of 96.4% for six different modulation formats of communication signals, and maintains excellent recognition accuracy under various signal-to-noise ratios. This research provides a new method for radio detection and spectrum management, contributing to the assurance of communication security.

articleTitle: Contrastive Learning Based Graph Convolution for Action Recognition
abstract: Skeleton-based human action recognition has the advantage of not being affected by background, light and other factors. Graph convolutional networks are usually used to extract the features in the skeleton graph. However, the feature points of some behaviors in the skeleton graph are very close to each other, and the ordinary graph convolutional network has poor ability to capture the relationship between distant nodes. In order to solve these two problems, by using the characteristics of G3D module that directly spreads information on the spatio-temporal graph, the idea of coordinate attention is introduced to enhance the model's ability to capture the relationship between distant nodes, so that the model can accurately retain local position information while capturing the strong dependence between two distant nodes. The contrastive learning method was introduced to enhance the feature expression ability of the neural network and improve the recognition accuracy of the model on similar actions. Through experiments, the proposed algorithm is compared with the original G3D model and other common algorithms on the NTU RGB-D dataset. The results show that the accuracy of the proposed algorithm is significantly improved than the original model on the NTU RGB-D dataset.

articleTitle: Research Progress of Human Movement Assessment System
abstract: The working principles and methods included in the existing motion estimation techniques are classified, and the research on motion estimation in various fields at home and abroad is collected in the existing literature to investigate and analyse the application of motion estimation in different fields as well as their respective advantages and limitations. Firstly, in terms of obtaining human movement information, two approaches are generally used: wearable sensor-based and vision-based pose estimation techniques. On this basis, the current methods of motion assessment are reviewed in terms of rule-based and model-based approaches, and then, the limitations of rule-based assessment methods are discussed and analysed, and it is pointed out that, with the development of technology and the increase of demand for personalised training, model-based scoring methods are more promising in the field of motion, and they can better solve the problem of evaluating and analyses. Finally, suggestions are made for future research directions.

articleTitle: Realizing Cattle and Sheep Target Detection in Ecological Livestock Farming Based on Improved YOLOv8 Model
abstract: With the advancement of AI and big data technology, the livestock industry in Qinghai Province has encountered a significant opportunity for livestock monitoring and management. The abundance of image data has provided a new driving force for economic development, but variations in lighting, background, and animal posture present challenges for target detection. To adapt to the plateau environment, continuous innovation and optimization of algorithms are necessary.In order to address the challenges in livestock monitoring, a large number of image data of cattle and sheep were collected through widespread deployment of cameras in Qinghai Province. After thorough investigation of YOLO series models, it was determined that YOLOv8 outperformed YOLOv5, YOLOv6, and YOLOv7 in accuracy while also demonstrating superior stability compared to YOLOv9. As a result, YOLOv8 was selected as the base model for optimization leading to the development of a new object detection model - YOLOV8-ZX. During the optimization process, several innovative strategies were implemented including selecting ODC-FPN as the backbone network to enhance feature extraction capability; introducing c2f-cam-Neck structure to improve recognition ability in complex backgrounds; unifying object detection head and integrating attention mechanism (Dy-Head)[2] which not only improved generalization performance but also significantly reduced computational complexity. These optimizations enabled YOLOv8-ZX to maintain excellent detection accuracy and stability even in complex and variable environments. Furthermore, introduction of attention mechanism enhanced network's ability to identify key features thereby improving accuracy and robustness of detection. Compared with YOLOV8 model alone,YOLOV8-ZX demonstrated 4.4% increase in mAP50 , 5.4% increase MAP50-95, and 3.7% decrease box damage . Experimental results indicate that optimizedYolo v8 model exhibits exceptional generalization performance & robustness when addressing livestock detection tasks within Qinghai province thus providing an efficient & practical technical solution for livestock monitoring. These research findings not only promote application computer vision within animal husbandry but also provide effective reference solutions similar target detections problems within similar environments.

articleTitle: The Improved Method for Gait Recognition Based on Human Body Contour Features
abstract: With the continuous deepening of deep learning methods in the field of image recognition, significant progress has been made in the research of human gait recognition algorithms. As a method capable of identifying unique biological features from a distance, human gait recognition finds extensive applications in areas such as public security investigation, medical rehabilitation, identity recognition, and smart homes. The Gaitset algorithm is primarily used for human gait recognition. However, due to its poor learning and weak classification abilities in the backbone network, there are limitations in feature extraction capabilities at different scales when using Gaitset to extract human silhouettes. As a result, the accuracy of gait recognition results is not high.This article proposes an improved method for gait recognition based on human silhouette features. By preprocessing the human silhouettes, it aims to extract contour shapes and dynamic features as comprehensively as possible. In addition, the ordinary convolutions in the Gaitset network are replaced with Inception modules to further enhance the network's representational capacity.Experimental verification was conducted on the publicly available CASIA-B dataset. The results of the experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an average recognition rate of 95.41% under normal walking conditions, 88.23% when carrying a backpack, and 70.42% when wearing a coat. Compared to the original Gaitset algorithm, the accuracy has been improved, with increases of 0.41%, 1.03%, and 0.07% respectively.The improved method effectively enhances the accuracy of human gait recognition, providing a more reliable and efficient solution for research in the field of human gait recognition.

articleTitle: Research and Application of Student Classroom Behavior Recognition Based on Deep Learning
abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence technology, computer vision technology has become an important means of obtaining behavioral information. However, the current student classroom behavior detection system still has the problem of low target detection accuracy. To improve students' learning efficiency in the classroom and reduce teachers' workload, this article proposes an improved YOLOv8 network model. The bounding box loss function is modified to Alpha-SIOU and the multi-dimensional collaborative attention mechanism MCA is introduced in front of the head to optimize the model. Experimental results show that when the detection rate and calculation amount of this model remain unchanged, compared with the original YOLOv8 model, the mAP value increases from the original 91% to 93%, the precision rate increases from the original 86.5% to 88.1%, and the recall rate increases from The original 84% increased to 88.3%. The improved model effectively improves the recognition accuracy and performs stably in complex detection environments, providing a valuable reference for classroom behavior detection research and smart classroom construction.

articleTitle: Research on gesture recognition method based on PSO optimized LSTM for surface muscle signals
abstract: (sEMG) Surface EMG signals can quickly and accurately reflect the movement intention of human body, gesture recognition by sEMG has been widely studied in the field of human-robot interaction in rehabilitation robots, in order to improve the accuracy of gesture recognition. A gesture recognition method based on PSO optimised LSTM for surface muscle signals is investigated. Firstly, the S_Dbw method is used to evaluate the clustering validity of the time domain features of the surface EMG signals, and the feature (MAV)combination of absolute mean +(RMS)root mean square (RMS)+ (VAR) variance is selected as the feature space and input to the model of the depth algorithm. Secondly, in order to solve the problem of cumbersome parameter debugging and low accuracy of (LSTM)Long Short-Term Memory neural network (LSTM), Particle Swarm Optimization-Long Short-Term Memory PSO-LSTM algorithm is proposed and combined with convolutional neural network (convolutional neural network, CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory LSTM. The experimental results show that the PSO-LSTM model has an average recognition accuracy of 94.1%, which is 8.3% and 4.7% higher than the CNN and LSTM, and the average training time of the LSTM model is reduced by 35.52s compared to the LSTM. Therefore, it is advantageous to use PSO-LSTM model in gesture sEMG signal recognition and classification.

articleTitle: Research on Pupil Center Localization Method Based on Fitting Elliptical Contours with Arc-support Line Segments
abstract: In head-mounted eye tracking system, detecting pupil center efficiently and precisely is the prime assignment. A pupil center localization method based on fitting elliptical contours with arc-support line segments is proposed to solve the problems of low detection rates of existing pupil detection algorithms in real-world scenarios caused by factors such as lighting variations, occlusions, and off-axis effects. First, use the Haar feature detector to locate the approximate position of the pupil in the eye diagram. Secondly, combine the Canny algorithm with the arc-support segment detection algorithm to extract the elliptical arc that may belong to the pupil contour, and eliminate a large number of redundant points. Then according to the distance, polarity and direction between the arc segments, the arc segments are combined into different groups, and ellipse fitting is performed by the Least Squares Method to generate the initial ellipse set. Based on the physiological characteristics of the pupil, filter out the ellipse with positive polarity, and determine the support inlier of the ellipse. Finally, the support inlier is fitted for a second time to obtain more accurate ellipse parameters, and the best ellipse is selected as the pupil contour according to the ellipse confidence level. Through comparative experiments on the public eye image dataset (LPW), the average detection rate has increased by 12.5% compared with the highest of the existing six algorithms, Even if the acquiring of eye image is affected by some shadows and light spots, the proposed method still can accurately identify the pupil, can be applied to various head-mounted eye tracking systems to provide more accurate pupil position information for line-of-sight estimation.

articleTitle: Identification Method of Electric Meter Reading Based on YOLOv7 and DCNN
abstract: Meter reading recognition is an essential indispensable part of intelligent grid inspection systems. However, due to limitations in the installation angles of monitoring cameras, captured images often suffer from angle issues, thereby reducing recognition accuracy. Therefore, this paper proposes a two-stage detection and recognition algorithm based on YOLOv7-tiny and DCNN networks. Firstly, the key point detection algorithm of YOLOv7 is improved by adding the EVC module, which enables the model to extract image features more comprehensively. Utilizing the Wingloss loss function, key point detection of meter reading regions is achieved. Then, perspective transformation is performed on the meter reading regions based on key point coordinate information to correct the images. Secondly, the deep convolutional neural network (DCNN-CTC) algorithm is employed for text recognition in images. Through extensive experiments with actual meter data, the results indicate that compared to YOLOv5 and CRNN methods, the proposed approach can recognize various meter reading information from different shooting angles with an increased accuracy rate of 5.8%.

articleTitle: Community Detection Algorithm Based On High-Order Variational Graph Autoencoder
abstract: The topic of community discovery algorithm has important research significance in complex network scientific research, and the acquisition of network topology structure information is one of its key research areas. With the exponential growth of community network size, there is not only the problem of dimensionality disaster, but also the difficulty of extracting sufficient community structure information. Obviously, the experimental performance of traditional community discovery algorithms is difficult to meet our needs in such an environment. At the same time, most existing models only use traditional adjacency matrices to obtain topological structure information. In response to the above problems, this paper proposes a community discovery algorithm (Aggregation-VGAE) based on variational graph autoencoders to obtain high-order topological structure information, extracting more accurate high-order topological structure information to find community structures more accurately. First, an aggregation matrix is generated by extracting the first-order and second-order structural information of the topological graph; secondly, a variational graph autoencoder is used to extract and reduce the dimensionality of the feature matrix containing network attributes to obtain a low-dimensional embedding matrix; finally, K- means clustering algorithm to obtain community structure information. We compare Aggregation-VGAE with the baseline model VGAE and its 7 other algorithms using the NMI evaluation metric on the citation network dataset. By evaluating the algorithm on a large real data set, the experimental results and visualization of the clustering results show that the Aggregation-VGAE algorithm has better community segmentation results in the citation network than other various algorithms.

articleTitle: Research on human movements push up counter based on media-pipe artificial intelligence
abstract: This paper introduces a project that integrates pose estimation and deep learning to evaluate exercise performance and provide real-time feedback on repetition counts during workouts. Using machine learning in the fitness sector, the study focuses on accurately tracking and counting exercise repetitions, which is beneficial for physical education and competitive fitness events. The paper presents a novel real-time push-up counting method based on 2D video analysis, utilizing Media-pipe for precise pose estimation and motion analysis. By following the push-up guidelines set by the National Academy of Sports Medicine, the method differentiates between correct and incorrect push-up forms. The experimental results show that the proposed method achieves an accuracy of 90.00%, precision of 91.67%, recall of 91.67%, and an F1-Score of 91.66%. The integration of pose estimation and deep learning in the fitness industry offers new opportunities for improving workout monitoring, ensuring proper form, and optimizing fitness outcomes for individuals of different fitness levels.

articleTitle: Method for Enhancing Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Target Detection in Challenging Environments Using Improved YOLOv8 Network
abstract: The intricate target sizes and fuzzy edges in Unmanned Aerial Vehicle(UAV) aerial images pose a great challenge for target detection. Therefore, investigating multiple recognition methods is crucial to solving the target detection problem of UAVs in challenging environments. In this study, the VisDrone2019 dataset is used, which contains high-resolution images under a variety of weather conditions and covers a number of challenging scenarios such as urban, suburban, and rural areas. In this paper, we propose a UAV aerial image detection and recognition method DAN-YOLOv8 based on the improved YOLOv8 network, which improves the detection performance of the model on UAV aerial images as well as the bounding box regression performance by replacing the convolutional part of the C2f module and redesigning the Neck part of the Backbone, as well as by introducing the Normalized Wasserstein Distance(NWD) loss function. After analyzing the UAV aerial images, it is observed that the detection model exhibits excellent environment perception and target recognition capabilities, which can simulate the intelligent features presented by humans when observing and analyzing images. The experimental results show that compared with other models, the network model proposed in this paper has a smaller number of parameters but higher accuracy, which significantly improves the detection performance and feature fusion ability of the model and enhances the detection efficiency and bounding-box regression performance for UAV aerial images. The results provide significant value and guidance for further development and application in the field of UAV target detection in challenging environments.
